answer: An agent network thwarts Sybil attacks through localized magneto-optical identity verification. Nodes record optical pulses from a survey lantern while measuring magnetic distortions from ferrous bedrock near a desert oasis. Because spatial gradients resist digital spoofing, adversaries must provision dedicated magnetometers and photodetectors per identity, imposing substantial hardware costs. However, sandstorms degrade optical line-of-sight, causing occasional false verification failures.
